feature: QUIC handshake caller-prepared RFC 8879 certificate compression
decision: reuse caller-prepared compressed Certificate bodies instead of building zlib state for every fresh connection
head: 8bce1753

attribution.method: CountingAllocator --capture-large=65536 return-address capture resolved with addr2line against the ReleaseFast binary
attribution.breakdown: 100 x 65,536-byte deflate work window and 100 x 230,096-byte std.compress.flate.Compress state

workload.tls: QUIC v1, TLS 1.3, pinned P-256 CertificateVerify

conclusion: The per-connection large allocations were zlib compressor setup for a 65-byte test certificate that cannot benefit from RFC 8879 framing. A matching caller-prepared view is now authoritative for its algorithm, so the handshake skips per-connection compression buffers when the prepared body does not save bytes, and reuses the prepared body when it does. Allocation bytes per handshake fell 77.1% and p50 handshake latency fell 29.5% in the same fixed binary.
